title: Equivalence of quantum resources under ergodic dynamics
authors: Sreemayee Aditya, Xhek Turkeshi, Piotr Sierant
abstract: Quantum resource theories characterize distinct forms of nonclassicality in many-body quantum states, raising the question of whether these resources evolve independently under generic ergodic dynamics. Considering diagnostics quadratic in the state, we show that the dynamics of different resource measures become mutually interdependent and are governed by a few common degrees of freedom. For Haar-random circuits, the purity together with a single resource witness suffices to reconstruct the remaining resource measures, as we demonstrate for coherence, various asymmetries, and number entropies. The same relations hold, to a good approximation, under chaotic Floquet and continuous-time Hamiltonian dynamics, establishing that this dynamical resource equivalence extends beyond random circuits. We further derive an exact coherence--imaginarity relation, remarkably accurate also beyond Haar-random circuits. Our results reveal an emergent simplification of many-body dynamics, in which sufficiently strong scrambling reduces seemingly distinct quantum resources to a few common dynamical degrees of freedom.
summary: The paper proves a profound 'dynamical resource equivalence' principle, demonstrating that various measures of nonclassicality are not independent under chaotic or random unitary evolution. By analyzing diagnostics quadratic in the state, the authors show that these resources can be largely reconstructed from just a few common dynamical variables, revealing an emergent simplification in complex quantum dynamics.
main_problem: The research investigates whether distinct quantum resource measures, which characterize nonclassicality, evolve independently under generic ergodic dynamics.
main_result: It is shown that these different resource measures become mutually interdependent and are governed by a few common dynamical degrees of freedom when considering quadratic state diagnostics. This equivalence extends from random circuits to chaotic Hamiltonian evolution.
method: The analysis uses the R\'enyi-2 relative-entropy formalism applied to various quantum resources (coherence, asymmetry) under dynamics simulated by Haar-random circuits, Floquet operators, and continuous Hamiltonians.
model_or_system: The study considers a chain of L qubits evolving via three ergodic dynamics: Haar-random brick-wall circuits, the Kicked Ising Model (KIM), and the Mixed-Field Ising Model (MFIM) Hamiltonian. The diagnostics are applied to subsystem A.
key_observables: Purity ($P$), Coherence ($C_d$), Imaginarity ($I(ho_A)$), and various Asymmetries ($\Delta S_G$).
important_parameters: The analysis is sensitive to the strength of scrambling, which dictates the emergence of dynamical equivalence.
main_assumptions: Key derivations rely on approximating the full spectral dynamics by its leading one-wall mode component, particularly in the context of Haar randomness.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate 'Dynamical Equivalence' showing how different resource measures are linked through common trajectories in state space for random circuits and Hamiltonian systems. Figure 7 specifically shows reconstruction across three ergodic dynamics.
paper_structure: The paper establishes a general framework by analyzing the evolution of quadratic diagnostics under various ergodic settings (random, Floquet, continuous). It derives specific mathematical relations showing that multiple resource measures can be reconstructed from just two or three fundamental quantities like purity and one other witness.
why_interesting: This work provides deep insight into how complex many-body dynamics simplify; the finding that seemingly distinct quantum resources collapse onto a few common dynamical degrees of freedom is highly relevant for understanding scrambling in strongly interacting systems.
